practicals.hazards: Sulphuric Acid, 0.5M (irritant), Copper oxide powder (Harmful), Copper sulfate (Product - Harmful), Bunsen Burner
practicals.risks: Skin irritation. Burns Products harmful to the environment

practicals.notes: When heating the copper(II) oxide and dilute sulfuric acid, avoid boiling off the water and allowing the copper sulfate to appear and then decompose with excessive heating – this is unsafe. The sulfur dioxide gases are toxic and can cause breathing difficulties. There may be problems associated with younger students heating beakers perched on tripods, and with lifting hot glassware off a hot tripod after heating. They should not be sitting down while carrying out these operations. Using tongs of suitable size is a good solution for lifting the hot beakers, but some schools may not have these. If there is any doubt about the safety of this step, you should assist students when lifting each beaker down onto the heat resistant mat.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Welcome to Human Biology: What do you already know?
lessons.subject: intro
lessons.notes: Course induction + knowledge baseline. Brief course/assessment overview, expectations, and 'what makes Human Biology different?'. Closed-book diagnostic sampling 30 marks across Cells (8), Tissues & Systems (6), Reproduction (5), Microbiology (5), and Scientific Maths (6). Targets OCR misconception patterns (bacterial cell ribosomes, mitochondria energy transfer vs production, DNA → ribosome → protein → ATP requirement sequence). Concludes with 5–6 diagnostic hinge questions.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Working like a Human Biologist
lessons.subject: intro
lessons.notes: Practical baseline diagnostic. Microscope set-up, preparing/examining temporary wet mounts (cheek & onion cells), focusing safely, scientific biological drawing with annotations, calculating magnification from measurements, identifying sources of error, and evaluating experimental methodology.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Thinking like a Human Biologist – Interpolation and extrapolation – Heart rate Practical
lessons.subject: intro
lessons.notes: Scientific maths, data and exam literacy diagnostic with live physiological data collection. Part A (15 marks Mathematics): Unit conversion (mm → μm → nm), magnification (image size ÷ actual size), standard form, percentage change, cell dimension ratios, graph interpretation/trend analysis including interpolation and extrapolation. Part B (Heart rate PAG): Students measure resting and post-exercise heart rate, plot data, and draw interpolated/extrapolated trend lines to practise key mathematical skills in a biological context.

practicals.notes: Resting vs post-exercise pulse, blood pressure, and pulse waveform analysis.

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Communicating like a Human Biologist: Sourcing & Harvard referencing
lessons.subject: intro
lessons.notes: Academic literature sourcing & Harvard referencing masterclass. Evaluating the credibility of scientific information; distinguishing peer-reviewed medical journals from commercial/secondary sources; assessing author authority, currency, sample sizes, and potential conflict of interest/bias; academic database search strategies (PubMed, Europe PMC, Google Scholar); constructing standard in-text citations and complete Harvard reference lists for journal papers, books, clinical trial registries, and NHS/NICE clinical guidelines.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Communicating like a Human Biologist: Interpreting data Clinical Trials
lessons.subject: intro
lessons.notes: Data interpretation, graphical analysis, and statistical literacy diagnostic using clinical trial datasets. Processing randomised controlled trial (RCT) outcomes and physiological datasets; interpreting error bars, standard deviation, and confidence intervals; evaluating relative risk reduction vs absolute risk reduction; identifying mathematical relationships (linear, exponential, saturation); evaluating validity, sources of systematic vs random error, and drawing evidence-based conclusions from biological data.

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Communicating like a Human Biologist: Academic writing & application
lessons.subject: intro
lessons.notes: Academic writing + evidence synthesis initial assessment. Controlled written task centered on an unfamiliar Human Biology stimulus (e.g. artificial organs clinical trial outcome data). Students extract and synthesize evidence, formulate structured biological explanations (fact → mechanism → clinical impact), correctly apply Harvard in-text citations, and complete evaluative conclusions to set a baseline for NEA and extended coursework.

lessons.title: Lesson 7: Introductory Unit Synthesis: Diagnostic Profile & Target Setting
lessons.subject: intro
lessons.notes: Triangulation of baseline diagnostic evidence across knowledge recall, scientific maths, microscope practical competence, and academic writing/data interpretation to set individual learner targets and NEA skill priorities.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Welcome to Human Biology: What do you already know?
lessons.subject: intro
lessons.notes: Course induction + knowledge baseline. Brief course/assessment overview, expectations, and 'what makes Human Biology different?'. Closed-book diagnostic sampling 30 marks across Cells (8), Tissues & Systems (6), Reproduction (5), Microbiology (5), and Scientific Maths (6). Targets OCR misconception patterns (bacterial cell ribosomes, mitochondria energy transfer vs production, DNA → ribosome → protein → ATP requirement sequence). Concludes with 5–6 diagnostic hinge questions.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Working like a Human Biologist
lessons.subject: intro
lessons.notes: Practical baseline diagnostic. lessons.title: Lesson 3: Thinking like a Human Biologist – Interpolation and extrapolation – Heart rate Practical
lessons.subject: intro
lessons.notes: Scientific maths, data and exam literacy diagnostic with live physiological data collection. Part A (15 marks Mathematics): Unit conversion (mm → μm → nm), magnification (image size ÷ actual size), standard form, percentage change, cell dimension ratios, graph interpretation/trend analysis including interpolation and extrapolation. Part B (Heart rate PAG): Students measure resting and post-exercise heart rate, plot data, and draw interpolated/extrapolated trend lines to practise key mathematical skills in a biological context.

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Communicating like a Human Biologist: Sourcing & Harvard referencing
lessons.subject: intro
lessons.notes: Academic literature sourcing & Harvard referencing masterclass. Evaluating the credibility of scientific information; distinguishing peer-reviewed medical journals from commercial/secondary sources; assessing author authority, currency, sample sizes, and potential conflict of interest/bias; academic database search strategies (PubMed, Europe PMC, Google Scholar); constructing standard in-text citations and complete Harvard reference lists for journal papers, books, clinical trial registries, and NHS/NICE clinical guidelines.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Communicating like a Human Biologist: Interpreting data Clinical Trials
lessons.subject: intro
lessons.notes: Data interpretation, graphical analysis, and statistical literacy diagnostic using clinical trial datasets. Processing randomised controlled trial (RCT) outcomes and physiological datasets; interpreting error bars, standard deviation, and confidence intervals; evaluating relative risk reduction vs absolute risk reduction; identifying mathematical relationships (linear, exponential, saturation); evaluating validity, sources of systematic vs random error, and drawing evidence-based conclusions from biological data.

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Communicating like a Human Biologist: Academic writing & application
lessons.subject: intro
lessons.notes: Academic writing + evidence synthesis initial assessment. Controlled written task centered on an unfamiliar Human Biology stimulus (e.g. artificial organs clinical trial outcome data). Students extract and synthesize evidence, formulate structured biological explanations (fact → mechanism → clinical impact), correctly apply Harvard in-text citations, and complete evaluative conclusions to set a baseline for NEA and extended coursework.

lessons.title: Lesson 7: Introductory Unit Synthesis: Diagnostic Profile & Target Setting
lessons.subject: intro
lessons.notes: Triangulation of baseline diagnostic evidence across knowledge recall, scientific maths, microscope practical competence, and academic writing/data interpretation to set individual learner targets and NEA skill priorities.

lessons.title: Lesson 8: Transition to Biomedical Science & Genetics
lessons.subject: intro
lessons.notes: Introduction to the linear curriculum structure: Genetics unit → Biomedical Techniques unit → Fundamentals of Human Biology unit. Overview of assessment routes, NEA task schedule, health & safety briefing for diagnostic reagents, and transition to Genetics Unit topics.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Unit intro & Phenotypic variation
lessons.subject: genetics
lessons.notes: Continuous vs discontinuous variation, normal distribution curves, and the interaction between polygenic inheritance and environmental factors.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Investigating phenotypic variation
lessons.subject: genetics
lessons.notes: Analyzing anthropometric phenotypic data, calculating standard deviation, and plotting biometrics.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: DNA structure, telomeres & replication
lessons.subject: genetics
lessons.notes: Antiparallel double helix structure, nucleotide phosphorylation, phosphodiester bonds, telomere attrition in human ageing, and semiconservative replication.

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Gene expression & transcriptional regulation
lessons.subject: genetics
lessons.notes: Promoter architecture, general and specific transcription factors, enhancers, silencers, and response elements.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Gene mutations: acquired and inherited
lessons.subject: genetics
lessons.notes: Point mutations (missense, nonsense, silent), frameshift insertions/deletions, mutagenic agents, and DNA repair mechanisms.

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Genetic disorders: single gene disorders
lessons.subject: genetics
lessons.notes: Aetiology, molecular pathology, and clinical presentation of Cystic Fibrosis (CFTR) and Sickle Cell Anaemia (HBB).

lessons.title: Lesson 7: Genetic disorders: Chromosomal abnormalities
lessons.subject: genetics
lessons.notes: Nondisjunction, aneuploidy karyotyping, Down's syndrome, Turner's syndrome, and Klinefelter's syndrome.

lessons.title: Lesson 8: Genetic disorders: Polygenic and complex traits
lessons.subject: genetics
lessons.notes: Multifactorial inheritance, genome-wide association studies (GWAS), polygenic risk scores, and environmental triggers.

lessons.title: Lesson 9: Gene therapy: viral & non-viral vector delivery
lessons.subject: genetics
lessons.notes: Adenoviral, lentiviral, and AAV vectors compared to liposomes, electroporation, and nanoparticle gene delivery.

lessons.title: Lesson 10: Gene therapy clinical trials & Task 2 research
lessons.subject: genetics
lessons.notes: Case studies of approved gene therapies (Luxturna, Zolgensma), clinical trial phases, and NEA Task 2 literature research.

lessons.title: Lesson 11: Genetic engineering compared to gene therapy
lessons.subject: genetics
lessons.notes: Recombinant DNA, transgenic organisms, somatic vs germline interventions, and regulatory boundaries.

lessons.title: Lesson 12: CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing & research workshop
lessons.subject: genetics
lessons.notes: gRNA design, PAM sequence recognition, Cas9 endonuclease cleavage, non-homologous end joining vs HDR, and off-target screening.

lessons.title: Lesson 13: The role & clinical scope of a genetic counsellor
lessons.subject: genetics
lessons.notes: Clinical genetic counselling pathways, multidisciplinary medical genetics teams, constructing multi-generational pedigree charts, and risk calculation.

lessons.title: Lesson 14: Mendelian inheritance: monohybrid crosses
lessons.subject: genetics
lessons.notes: Autosomal dominant and recessive inheritance models, Punnett squares, and probability calculations.

lessons.title: Lesson 15: Genetic tests: diagnostic, carrier & predictive
lessons.subject: genetics
lessons.notes: Targeted single-gene sequencing, gene panels, diagnostic indications, asymptomatic carrier screening, and predictive testing in adult-onset conditions.

lessons.title: Lesson 16: Sex-linked inheritance & codominance calculations
lessons.subject: genetics
lessons.notes: X-linked recessive disorders (haemophilia, Duchenne muscular dystrophy), codominance (ABO blood antigens), and pedigree tracking.

lessons.title: Lesson 17: Statistical testing in genetics: Chi-squared analysis
lessons.subject: genetics
lessons.notes: Formulating null hypotheses, degrees of freedom, calculating chi-squared test statistics, and critical value tables.

lessons.title: Lesson 18: Genetic tests in adults and PGD screening
lessons.subject: genetics
lessons.notes: Pre-implantation genetic diagnosis (PGD) in IVF, carrier screening in prospective parents, and adult predictive testing.

lessons.title: Lesson 19: Genetic tests: prenatal amniocentesis & CVS
lessons.subject: genetics
lessons.notes: Chorionic villus sampling (CVS) vs amniocentesis, cell-free fetal DNA (NIPT), clinical risks, and diagnostic accuracy.

lessons.title: Lesson 20: Privacy, ethics & data governance in genetic banking
lessons.subject: genetics
lessons.notes: Genetic privacy, GDPR, ownership of human genomic sequence data, commercial direct-to-consumer testing, and health insurance discrimination.

lessons.title: Lesson 21: Genetics NEA: Clinical genetics case studies & research design
lessons.subject: genetics
lessons.notes: Formulating individual patient case profiles, evaluating family histories, and designing clinical diagnostic investigation plans.

lessons.title: Lesson 22: Genetics NEA: Pedigree chart analysis & risk calculation
lessons.subject: genetics
lessons.notes: Formal standardized pedigree nomenclature, Bayesian conditional probability calculations, and empirical recurrence risk tables.

lessons.title: Lesson 23: Genetics NEA: Genomic databases & variant annotation
lessons.subject: genetics
lessons.notes: Navigating ClinVar, OMIM, Ensembl, and gnomAD to classify variants of uncertain significance (VUS) and pathogenic mutations.

lessons.title: Lesson 24: Genetics NEA: Ethical dilemmas in gene editing & screening
lessons.subject: genetics
lessons.notes: Synthesizing bioethical frameworks (autonomy, non-maleficence, beneficence, justice) applied to reproductive choices and somatic gene editing.

lessons.title: Lesson 25: Genetics NEA Task 3: Genomic data processing & analysis
lessons.subject: genetics
lessons.notes: Analyzing Sanger sequencing chromatograms, next-generation sequencing read depths, and variant consequence calling.

lessons.title: Lesson 26: Genetics NEA Task 3: Clinical interpretation & report write-up
lessons.subject: genetics
lessons.notes: Interpreting genetic assay findings against clinical phenotypes, ACMG variant classification guidelines, and drafting diagnostic report.

lessons.title: Lesson 27: Genetics NEA Task 3: Diagnostic conclusion & patient recommendations
lessons.subject: genetics
lessons.notes: Synthesizing full clinical diagnostic report with management strategies, cascade testing recommendations, and referenced literature.

lessons.title: Lesson 28: Genetics Unit Review & NEA synthesis
lessons.subject: genetics
lessons.notes: Synoptic consolidation of molecular genetics, inheritance patterns, counselling protocols, and final submission audit.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: The purpose of biomedical science
lessons.subject: biomedical
lessons.notes: Roles in NHS pathology services, ISO 15189 accreditation, clinical governance, and diagnostic patient pathways.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Biomedical science careers: Haematology & Microscopy
lessons.subject: biomedical
lessons.notes: Haematology, histopathology, medical microbiology, clinical biochemistry, and blood transfusion services.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Handling Specimens: chain of custody & safety
lessons.subject: biomedical
lessons.notes: COSHH regulations, Category 1-4 biohazard containment, specimen barcoding, and chain of custody.

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Reference values & population statistics (FBC)
lessons.subject: biomedical
lessons.notes: Full blood count (FBC) parameters, reference ranges, 95% confidence intervals, and biological variation.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Haematology & Blood typing in diagnosis
lessons.subject: biomedical
lessons.notes: ABO and RhD forward & reverse blood grouping, agglutination reactions, crossmatching, and transfusion safety.

practicals.title: Haematology & Blood typing simulation
practicals.hazards: Simulated blood serums (anti-A, anti-B, anti-Rh)
practicals.precautions: Wear gloves, lab coat, and eye protection.
practicals.notes: Synthetic blood samples for ABO and Rh typing investigation.

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Separation techniques & inorganic ion tests
lessons.subject: biomedical
lessons.notes: Thin-layer chromatography (TLC) of amino acids and qualitative precipitate reactions for diagnostic inorganic ions.

practicals.title: Thin Layer Chromatography (TLC)
practicals.hazards: Chromatography solvent, capillary tubes, UV light
practicals.precautions: Use in well-ventilated room or fume hood. Wear protective gloves.
practicals.notes: Separation of biological pigments and amino acids using TLC plates.

lessons.title: Lesson 7: Urinalysis with Reagent test strips
lessons.subject: biomedical
lessons.notes: Biochemical analysis of urine using multilayer dipsticks for glucose, ketones, protein, bilirubin, and specific gravity.

practicals.title: Urinalysis with reagent test strips
practicals.hazards: Simulated urine samples, test strips
practicals.precautions: Wear disposable gloves and lab coat. Dispose of strips in designated waste.
practicals.notes: Testing for glucose, protein, ketones, and pH in patient case studies.

lessons.title: Lesson 8: Biomedical NEA TASK 1: Literature search & review
lessons.subject: biomedical
lessons.notes: Systematic literature search methodology using PubMed and Google Scholar, source appraisal, and Harvard referencing.

lessons.title: Lesson 9: Biomedical NEA TASK 1: Qualitative tests & Colorimetry
lessons.subject: biomedical
lessons.notes: Constructing standard calibration curves with spectrophotometry (Beer-Lambert law) and protein quantification.

practicals.title: Colorimetry and Spectrophotometry
practicals.hazards: Biuret reagent, Benedict's reagent, cuvettes
practicals.precautions: Wear eye protection and gloves. Handle cuvettes by ribbed sides.
practicals.notes: Constructing serial dilutions and calibration curve for concentration determination.

lessons.title: Lesson 10: Qualitative tests for inorganic ions
lessons.subject: biomedical
lessons.notes: Confirming presence of calcium, iron, chloride, and phosphate in physiological and pathological fluid models.

lessons.title: Lesson 11: Quantitative tests: Volumetric acid-base titration
lessons.subject: biomedical
lessons.notes: Volumetric titration to quantify acid-base imbalances (metabolic acidosis model) with precision glassware.

practicals.title: Volumetric acid-base titration
practicals.hazards: Acids, alkalis, burettes, indicators
practicals.precautions: Wear goggles and lab coat. Fill burette below eye level using funnel.
practicals.notes: Standardisation and concentration analysis using volumetric titration.

lessons.title: Lesson 12: Biomedical NEA TASK 1: Data review & write-up
lessons.subject: biomedical
lessons.notes: Synthesising calibration data, calculating unknown concentrations, error budgeting, and scientific reporting.

lessons.title: Lesson 13: Microbiology in diagnosis including Gram staining
lessons.subject: biomedical
lessons.notes: Aseptic technique, smear heat-fixation, crystal violet/iodine/decolorizer/safranin protocol, and optical microscopy.

practicals.title: Microbiology & Gram staining
practicals.hazards: Crystal violet, Gram's iodine, safranin, ethanol, bacterial culture
practicals.precautions: Aseptic technique near Bunsen flame. Wear lab coat and nitrile gloves.
practicals.notes: Gram positive vs Gram negative differentiation under oil immersion microscopy.

lessons.title: Lesson 14: Electrophoresis, biopsy techniques & ELISA assays
lessons.subject: biomedical
lessons.notes: Agarose and SDS-PAGE gel electrophoresis, needle core vs punch biopsy protocols, and indirect/sandwich ELISA.

lessons.title: Lesson 15: Planning an investigation: Methods & risk assessments
lessons.subject: biomedical
lessons.notes: Writing standard operating procedures (SOP), identifying independent/dependent/controlled variables, and HAZCHEM risk assessment.

lessons.title: Lesson 16: Analysis of data, errors & % uncertainty
lessons.subject: biomedical
lessons.notes: Distinguishing random vs systematic errors, calculating percentage uncertainties in volumetric and gravimetric glassware.

lessons.title: Lesson 17: Biomedical NEA TASK 2: Experimental design
lessons.subject: biomedical
lessons.notes: Student-led experimental plan for Task 2 practical investigation, selecting controls, and drafting SOP.

lessons.title: Lesson 18: Practice Task 1: Performing experimental protocol
lessons.subject: biomedical
lessons.notes: Executing analytical investigation under supervised laboratory conditions with calibrated instruments.

lessons.title: Lesson 19: Practice Task 2: Data processing & graphical analysis
lessons.subject: biomedical
lessons.notes: Plotting Michaelis-Menten kinetics and calibration curves, calculating gradients, standard error, and R-squared.

lessons.title: Lesson 20: Biomedical NEA TASK 2: Methodology evaluation
lessons.subject: biomedical
lessons.notes: Critiquing analytical sensitivity, specificity, repeatability, reproducibility, and procedural limitations.

lessons.title: Lesson 21: Biomedical NEA TASK 2: Practical data collection
lessons.subject: biomedical
lessons.notes: Recording raw experimental observations in laboratory notebooks following Good Laboratory Practice (GLP).

lessons.title: Lesson 22: Practice Task 3: Statistical testing & uncertainty
lessons.subject: biomedical
lessons.notes: Carrying out unpaired t-tests, calculating percentage error vs percentage uncertainty, and verifying hypotheses.

lessons.title: Lesson 23: Practice Task 4: Feedback & NEA finalisation
lessons.subject: biomedical
lessons.notes: Incorporating teacher formative feedback on draft practical reports and refining discussion sections.

lessons.title: Lesson 24: Biomedical NEA TASK 1: Submission & review
lessons.subject: biomedical
lessons.notes: Final audit of NEA Task 1 research submissions and verification of referenced clinical sources.

lessons.title: Lesson 25: Biomedical NEA TASK 3: Analytical processing
lessons.subject: biomedical
lessons.notes: Processing complex diagnostic patient datasets, normalizing biomarkers, and identifying abnormal physiological values.

lessons.title: Lesson 26: Biomedical NEA TASK 3: Statistical validation
lessons.subject: biomedical
lessons.notes: Performing t-tests, Mann-Whitney U tests, and correlation analysis between biomarker levels and disease severity.

lessons.title: Lesson 27: Biomedical NEA TASK 3: Final report write-up & diagnostic conclusion
lessons.subject: biomedical
lessons.notes: Finalising full NEA Task 3 diagnostic report with medical terminology, citations, figure legends, and clinical recommendations.

lessons.title: Lesson 28: Biomedical NEA TASK 4: Quality assurance review & Unit Review
lessons.subject: biomedical
lessons.notes: Internal quality control (IQC) schemes in ISO-accredited hospital laboratories, complete Biomedical Science NEA portfolio indexing, and synoptic synthesis.

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Relationships of organelles and cytoskeleton
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Microtubules, intermediate filaments, and actin microfilaments in intracellular transport, spindle formation, and cell motility.

lessons.title: Lesson 7: Biological drawing skills & scale calculations
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Standardized biological drawing conventions, scale bars, and calculating actual cell sizes from micrographs.

lessons.title: Lesson 8: Prokaryotes vs eukaryotes comparison
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Structural distinctions including naked circular DNA, 70S vs 80S ribosomes, murein cell walls, and binary fission kinetics.

lessons.title: Lesson 9: Role of Cell membranes & Fluid mosaic model
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Phospholipid bilayer fluidity, cholesterol modulation, integral transport proteins, and glycoprotein cell recognition markers.

lessons.title: Lesson 10: Factors affecting membrane structure & permeability
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Thermodynamic and solvent disruption of cell membranes, protein denaturation, and leakage of cellular contents.

lessons.title: Lesson 11: PAG - Factors affecting membrane structure
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Quantitative colorimetric assay measuring pigment leakage from Beta vulgaris tissue discs under varying temperatures.

practicals.title: Factors affecting membrane structure (PAG B4)
practicals.hazards: Hot water baths, ethanol solvent, cork borer
practicals.risks: Scalding, cuts from cork borer, flammable solvents
practicals.precautions: Use forceps/tongs for water baths. Keep ethanol away from naked flames.
practicals.notes: Beetroot cell membrane permeability under varying temperature and alcohol concentrations.

lessons.title: Lesson 12: Movement across membranes: diffusion & active transport
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Fick's law, facilitated diffusion via channel and carrier proteins, and primary/secondary ATP-driven active transport.

lessons.title: Lesson 13: Active and bulk transport, osmosis fundamentals
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Endocytosis, exocytosis, vesicle trafficking, water potential gradients, and osmotic pressure dynamics.

lessons.title: Lesson 14: Osmosis - practical investigation
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Determining the water potential of plant storage tissue using percentage mass change across a graded sucrose series.

practicals.title: Osmosis in plant tissue (PAG B2)
practicals.hazards: Cork borer, scalpel, sucrose solutions
practicals.risks: Cuts from scalpel or cork borer
practicals.precautions: Cut onto a white tile using downward pressure. Wear safety glasses.
practicals.notes: Potato cylinders in sucrose series (0.0M to 1.0M).

lessons.title: Lesson 15: Stem cells & Electron microscopy
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Pluripotent, multipotent and totipotent stem cell lineages, therapeutic cloning, and transmission vs scanning electron microscopy.

lessons.title: Lesson 16: DNA, Chromosomes & Initial Assessment Review
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Higher-order chromatin packaging around histone octamers, chromosome anatomy, milestone findings of the Human Genome Project, and comprehensive review of the Unit 1 initial-assessment diagnostic profile.

lessons.title: Lesson 17: Cell Biology Synthesis & Transition to Human Physiology
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Synoptic consolidation linking cell ultrastructure and membrane transport kinetics to macroscopic human organ system functions.

lessons.title: Lesson 18: Anatomy of the Brain
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Introduction to the key regions of the brain, including the skull, meninges, cerebrum, cerebellum, Hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis, and the brain stem (pons, medulla, midbrain).

lessons.title: Lesson 19: Modelling Brain Anatomy
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Focus on interpreting photographic scans (CT/MRI). Students practice drawing fully annotated, low-power plan diagrams of transverse and vertical sections of the brain, and discuss the challenges the skull and meninges present during brain surgery.

lessons.title: Lesson 20: The Spinal Cord
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Exploration of the spinal cord's transverse section (vertebrae, meninges, grey/white matter, central canal). Discussion of clinical procedures like lumbar punctures, and why cervical breaks are more damaging than lumbar breaks.

lessons.title: Lesson 21: Nerve Anatomy and Injury
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Microscopic study of cranial and spinal nerves (endoneurium, perineurium, epineurium, fascicles, and myelin sheath). Analysis of how repetitive sports injuries or traumatic injuries lead to a loss of motor and sensory functions.

lessons.title: Lesson 22: Circulatory system: blood vessel structure
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Elastic arteries, muscular arteries, arterioles, capillary beds, venules, and veins in regulating blood pressure and peripheral resistance.

lessons.title: Lesson 23: Measuring heart activity: ECG & Blood Pressure
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Recording and interpreting normal sinus rhythm ECG waveforms (P-wave, QRS-complex, T-wave), heart rate calculations, and sphygmomanometer blood pressure measurement.

practicals.title: Measuring cardiovascular activity & ECG
practicals.hazards: Stethoscopes, sphygmomanometers, pulse sensors
practicals.risks: Low risk, hygiene of shared ear pieces
practicals.precautions: Alcohol wipe stethoscopes before and after use.
practicals.notes: Resting vs post-exercise pulse, blood pressure, and pulse waveform analysis.

lessons.title: Lesson 24: Respiratory system: alveolar gas exchange
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Alveolar histology, pulmonary surfactant, Fick's law of diffusion, and mechanics of thoracic pressure changes during ventilation.

lessons.title: Lesson 25: Measuring lung activity: Spirometry & Peak Flow
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Measuring tidal volume, inspiratory/expiratory reserve volumes, vital capacity, FEV1, and peak flow in healthy vs compromised airways.

practicals.title: Measuring lung function: Spirometry & Peak Flow
practicals.hazards: Peak flow meters, disposable mouthpieces, spirometer
practicals.precautions: Use single-use disposable mouthpieces. Clean meters between sessions.
practicals.notes: Measuring tidal volume, vital capacity, and peak expiratory flow rate.

lessons.title: Lesson 26: Overview of the brain & nervous system
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Anatomical divisions: central (CNS) vs peripheral (PNS), somatic vs autonomic (sympathetic/parasympathetic) nervous systems.

lessons.title: Lesson 27: Musculoskeletal system & joint biomechanics
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Synovial joint architecture, cartilage, ligaments, tendons, antagonistic muscle pairs, and lever systems in human movement.

lessons.title: Lesson 28: Musculoskeletal diseases & ultrasound imaging
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Osteoarthritis, osteoporosis, fracture repair cascades, and medical ultrasound for soft tissue and musculoskeletal diagnostic imaging.

lessons.title: Lesson 29: Action potentials, nerve impulses & reflex arcs
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Resting membrane potential (-70mV), voltage-gated sodium/potassium channels, saltatory conduction, and monosynaptic vs polysynaptic reflex arcs.

lessons.title: Lesson 30: Synaptic transmission & neurotransmitters
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Cholinergic synapse function, acetylcholine synthesis and breakdown by acetylcholinesterase, and summation (temporal and spatial).

lessons.title: Lesson 31: Drug Impacts on Synapses
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Investigating how different pharmacological agents alter synaptic transmission by acting as agonists, antagonists, reuptake inhibitors, and enzyme activators.

lessons.title: Lesson 32: Neurodegenerative Diseases & Seizures
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Loss of dopaminergic neurons in Parkinson's disease, beta-amyloid plaques in Alzheimer's, and abnormal hypersynchronous neuronal firing in epileptic seizures.

lessons.title: Lesson 33: Movement, Balance & Cerebellar Control
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Motor cortex conscious movement planning, cerebellar coordination, vestibular apparatus, and proprioceptive muscle spindle feedback.

lessons.title: Lesson 34: Lymphatic system & fluid homeostasis
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Capillary fluid exchange, hydrostatic vs oncotic pressure, lymph formation, lymph node filtration, and secondary lymphedema.

lessons.title: Lesson 35: Gastrointestinal system: digestion mechanics
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Peristalsis, gastric secretion, enzyme kinetics (pepsins, amylases, lipases), and mucosal protective barriers.

lessons.title: Lesson 36: Gastrointestinal system: absorption & microbiome
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Villi and microvilli brush border co-transport of glucose and amino acids, lipid micelle absorption, and symbiotic gut microbiome roles.

lessons.title: Lesson 37: The Pancreas: endocrine & exocrine pathology
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Islets of Langerhans alpha/beta cells versus acinar exocrine enzyme secretion, pancreatitis, and pancreatic carcinoma.

lessons.title: Lesson 38: The Liver: metabolism & detoxification
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Hepatic lobule histology, deamination, urea cycle, cytochrome P450 drug metabolism, glycogen storage, and cirrhosis.

lessons.title: Lesson 39: Urinary system: nephron ultrafiltration
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Glomerular basement membrane podocytes, filtration pressure, selective proximal tubule reabsorption, and loop of Henle countercurrent multiplier.

lessons.title: Lesson 40: Diseases of the urinary system & kidney failure
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Glomerulonephritis, acute kidney injury (AKI), chronic kidney disease (CKD), haemodialysis versus peritoneal dialysis principles.

lessons.title: Lesson 41: Organ transplants & artificial organs
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: HLA tissue matching, hyperacute/acute graft rejection mechanisms, calcineurin inhibitors, and bioengineered artificial organ advances.

lessons.title: Lesson 42: Endocrine system: hormone signalling loops
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Peptide vs steroid hormone signalling, second messenger cascades (cAMP), pituitary-hypothalamic endocrine control axis.

lessons.title: Lesson 43: Homeostasis: negative feedback fundamentals
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Receptors, control centres, effectors, physiological tolerance ranges, and feedforward versus negative feedback mechanisms.

lessons.title: Lesson 44: Thermoregulation: autonomic responses
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Preoptic hypothalamic thermal monitoring, cutaneous vasodilation/vasoconstriction, piloerection, shivering, and sweat evaporation heat loss.

lessons.title: Lesson 45: Osmoregulation: ADH mechanism & hydration
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Hypothalamic osmoreceptors, posterior pituitary ADH (vasopressin) release, aquaporin-2 insertion into collecting duct membranes.

lessons.title: Lesson 46: Osmoregulation: renal electrolyte balance
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Aldosterone, renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS), atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP), and sodium/potassium ion homeostasis.

lessons.title: Lesson 47: Glucose homeostasis: diabetes mellitus
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Insulin-stimulated GLUT4 translocation, glucagon gluconeogenesis/glycogenolysis, Type 1 vs Type 2 diabetes pathophysiology.

lessons.title: Lesson 48: Clinical monitoring of glucose & biosensors
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM), glucose oxidase biosensors, amperometric current detection, and HbA1c glycated haemoglobin.

lessons.title: Lesson 49: Meiosis, independent assortment & recombination
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Homologous chromosome pairing, crossing over at chiasmata, random assortment, and non-disjunction origins.

lessons.title: Lesson 50: Female reproductive anatomy & oogenesis
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Ovarian histology, primordial follicle maturation, primary vs secondary oocytes, polar bodies, and ovulation mechanisms.

lessons.title: Lesson 51: Virology: structure, replication & antivirals
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Enveloped vs non-enveloped viral capsids, lytic vs lysogenic cycles, retroviral reverse transcriptase, and neuraminidase inhibitors.

lessons.title: Lesson 52: Collecting bacterial samples
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Sterile environmental swabbing, aseptic agar plate inoculation, serial dilution plating, and colony morphology evaluation.

practicals.title: Collecting & culturing environmental bacterial samples
practicals.hazards: Nutrient agar plates, sterile swabs, incubator
practicals.precautions: Tape agar plates closed with cross-taping. Incubate at max 25°C. Never open grown plates.
practicals.notes: Sampling surfaces and assessing microbial diversity.

lessons.title: Lesson 53: Hormonal control of menstrual cycles
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Interplay of GnRH, FSH, LH surge, oestrogen, and progesterone across follicular, ovulatory, and luteal phases.

lessons.title: Lesson 54: The Menopause & hormone replacement therapy
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Ovarian follicle depletion, declining oestrogen/inhibin, elevated gonadotropins, vasomotor symptoms, and HRT benefits vs risks.

lessons.title: Lesson 55: Bacterial reproduction & growth kinetics
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Binary fission generation time, bacterial growth phases (lag, log, stationary, death), and spectrophotometric optical density (OD600).

lessons.title: Lesson 56: Medical mycology, gut therapeutics & male reproductive anatomy
lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Yeasts vs filamentous dermatophytes, gut microbiome SCFA production, and male reproductive anatomy & spermatogenesis.

lessons.subject: fundamentals
lessons.notes: Comprehensive synoptic integration across cellular biology, diagnostic pathology algorithms, and clinical genetics case studies.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Welcome to Human Biology: What do you already know?
lessons.subject: intro
lessons.notes: Course induction + knowledge baseline. Brief course/assessment overview, expectations, and 'what makes Human Biology different?'. Closed-book diagnostic sampling 30 marks across Cells (8), Tissues & Systems (6), Reproduction (5), Microbiology (5), and Scientific Maths (6). Targets OCR misconception patterns (bacterial cell ribosomes, mitochondria energy transfer vs production, DNA → ribosome → protein → ATP requirement sequence). Concludes with 5–6 diagnostic hinge questions.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Thinking like a Human Biologist
lessons.subject: intro
lessons.notes: Scientific maths, data and exam literacy diagnostic. Part A (15 marks Mathematics): Unit conversion (mm → μm → nm), magnification (image size ÷ actual size), standard form, percentage change, cell dimension ratios, and graph interpretation/trend analysis. Part B (Exam literacy): Differentiating fact → explanation → consequence across short response items (ribosome function, binary fission, smooth muscle in digestive tract, and healthcare intervention scenario evaluation).

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Working like a Human Biologist
lessons.subject: intro
lessons.notes: Practical baseline diagnostic. Microscope set-up, preparing/examining temporary wet mounts (cheek & onion cells), focusing safely, scientific biological drawing with annotations, calculating magnification from measurements, identifying sources of error, and evaluating experimental methodology.

practicals.title: Onion and cheek cell microscopy (PAG B1)
practicals.hazards: Glass slides, methylene blue, iodine stain
practicals.precautions: Wear goggles and lab coat. Handle microscope slides with care.
practicals.notes: Practical baseline diagnostic: Microscope setup, cheek and onion slide preparation, biological drawing, and magnification calculation from OCR practical guidance.

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Communicating like a Human Biologist: Sourcing & Harvard referencing
lessons.subject: intro
lessons.notes: Academic literature sourcing & Harvard referencing masterclass. Evaluating the credibility of scientific information; distinguishing peer-reviewed medical journals from commercial/secondary sources; assessing author authority, currency, sample sizes, and potential conflict of interest/bias; academic database search strategies (PubMed, Europe PMC, Google Scholar); constructing standard in-text citations and complete Harvard reference lists for journal papers, books, clinical trial registries, and NHS/NICE clinical guidelines.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Communicating like a Human Biologist: Interpreting data
lessons.subject: intro
lessons.notes: Data interpretation, graphical analysis, and statistical literacy diagnostic. Processing clinical trial outcomes and physiological datasets; interpreting error bars, standard deviation, and confidence intervals; identifying mathematical relationships (linear, exponential, saturation); evaluating validity, sources of systematic vs random error, and drawing evidence-based conclusions from biological data.

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Communicating like a Human Biologist: Academic writing & application
lessons.subject: intro
lessons.notes: Academic writing + evidence synthesis initial assessment. Controlled written task centered on an unfamiliar Human Biology stimulus (e.g. artificial organs clinical trial outcome data). Students extract and synthesize evidence, formulate structured biological explanations (fact → mechanism → clinical impact), correctly apply Harvard in-text citations, and complete evaluative conclusions to set a baseline for NEA and extended coursework.
